'''''Kunzea robusta''''', commonly known as '''rawirinui''' or '''kānuka''',{{ref|a}} is a tree in the myrtle [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Myrtaceae]], and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to New Zealand. It has rough, stringy, or corky bark, lance-shaped leaves that are darker on the upper surface, flowers in compact groups of up to 30, each with five or six white [[petal]]s, and about 35 [[stamen]]s of varying lengths.

==Description==
''Kunzea robusta'' is a spreading shrub or tree, typically growing to a height of {{convert|20-30|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} with rough, stringy, or [[Tessellation|tessellated]] bark, which peels upward in long strips. The leaves are dark green above, paler below, lance-shaped, varying in size from  {{convert|3.2 to 28|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, from {{convert|0.7 to 2.5|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide, and [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]] or with a short [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]]. The flowers are white and arranged in compact groups of up to thirty, each flower on a [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] {{convert|1-5|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long. The [[Hypanthium|floral cup]] is conical to top-shaped or cup-shaped, with five papery [[sepal]]s about {{convert|0.5-1|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and wide. There are five or six egg-shaped to almost round [[petal]]s {{convert|1.5-4|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and wide. Between 15 and 60 [[stamen]]s, some slightly longer than the petals and others much shorter are arranged in two indistinct rows around the floral cup. Flowering occurs between April and June and is followed by fruit, which is a hairy, conical to more or less top-shaped [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]] {{convert|2.2-4.6|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|3.2-5.3|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide. The capsule usually opens to release its seed when mature.<ref name="NZPCN" /><ref name="PhytoKeys">{{cite journal|last1=de Lange|first1=Peter J.|title=A revision of the New Zealand ''Kunzea ericoides'' (Myrtaceae) complex|journal=PhytoKeys|date=2014|issue=40|pages=1–185|url=https://phytokeys.pensoft.net/article/1924/list/8/|access-date=1 April 2019|doi=10.3897/phytokeys.40.7973|pmid=25197228|pmc=4154306 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Kunzea robusta'' was first formally described in 2014 by New Zealand botanist [[Peter James de Lange]] from a specimen he collected near [[Papatea Bay]]. The description was published in ''[[PhytoKeys]]''.<ref name="ipni">{{IPNI| id = 77141733-1 | taxon = ''Kunzea robusta'' | access-date = 1 April 2019}}</ref> The [[Botanical nomenclature|specific epithet]] (''robusta'') is a [[Latin]] word meaning "hard and strong like oak",<ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.|page =766}}</ref> referring to the stature of mature trees of this species.<ref name="PhytoKeys" /> The taxonomic revision of the ''Kunzea ericoides'' complex by de Lange identified ''Kunzea robusta'' as a new species,<ref name="PhytoKeys" /> but a more recent analysis of the ''Kunzea'' complex observed little genetic variation and morphological distinction between the species, questioning the evidence for 10 endemic ''Kunzea'' species and suggesting further revision.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Heenan|first1=Peter B.|last2=McGlone|first2=Matt S.|last3=Mitchell|first3=Caroline M.|last4=Cheeseman|first4=Dagmar F.|last5=Houliston|first5=Gary J.|date=2021-04-07|title=Genetic variation reveals broad-scale biogeographic patterns and challenges species' classification in the ''Kunzea ericoides'' (kānuka; Myrtaceae) complex from New Zealand|url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0028825X.2021.1903946|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=60 |language=en|pages=2–26|doi=10.1080/0028825X.2021.1903946|s2cid=234860363 |issn=0028-825X|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

''Kānuka'' more often refers to ''[[Kunzea ericoides]]''; it is a [[Doublet (linguistics)|doublet]] of ''[[Leptospermum scoparium|mānuka]]'' from [[Proto-Polynesian language|Proto-Polynesian]] *''nukanuka'' or *''nuka'' which originally refers to ''[[Decaspermum]] fructicosum'' due to its similar small white flowers.<ref>{{cite web|website=Te Māra Reo|url=http://www.temarareo.org/PPN-Manuka.html|title=*Nuka, *Nukanuka, *-nuka|date=2022|access-date=30 October 2022|publisher=Benson Family Trust}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
Rawirinui is widespread and common on both the [[North Island|North]] and [[South Island]]s of New Zealand, and has often been confused with ''[[Kunzea ericoides|K. ericoides]]''.  It is mostly found in coastal and low-lying areas and nearby hilly country, especially around forest margins, and does not usually grow in upper [[Montane ecosystems|montane]] locations.<ref name="NZPCN" /><ref name="PhytoKeys" />

==Notes==
:1.{{note|a}} Although "kānuka" is considered an alternative to rawirinui,<ref name="NZPCN">{{cite web |last1=de Lange |first1=Peter James |title=''Kunzea robusta'' |url=http://www.nzpcn.org.nz/flora_details.aspx?ID=7644 |publisher=New Zealand Plant Conservation Network |access-date=1 April 2019}}</ref> it is much more commonly used to refer to ''[[Kunzea ericoides]]'', as described [[#Taxonomy and naming|above]].
